pl-l3d14c1-d1e117.summary: Asks, since Christ's soul was wise by gratuitous wisdom, whether it had wisdom equal to God's, or knows all things that God knows.

pl-l3d14c1-d1e120.summary: Reports a view that it neither has knowledge equal to God's nor knows all that God knows, since no creature is equal to the Creator in anything; that soul is a creature, so it is not equal in wisdom and does not know all God knows.
claims: On one view, no creature equals the Creator in anything, including knowledge.

pl-l3d14c1-d1e123.summary: Adds their argument: if that soul had wisdom equal to God's, God would not have greater sufficiency in every good than his creature.
claims: Argument: God must exceed every creature in every good.

pl-l3d14c1-d1e127.summary: Adds their authority, Ps 138:6 spoken in the person of the assumed man, 'your knowledge has become wonderful to me, I cannot reach it', which Cassiodorus expounds as showing that the assumed man cannot equal the divine substance in knowledge or anything else.
claims: The assumed man cannot equal the divine substance in knowledge.

pl-l3d14c1-d1e139.summary: Adds the Apostle: no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God, who alone searches all things, even the depths of God (1 Cor 2:10–11).
claims: Only the Spirit knows the depths of God.

pl-l3d14c1-d1e145.summary: Sums up their position and adds an argument: if Christ's soul knew all God knows, it would know how to create the world, and even how to create itself.
claims: Argument: knowing all would mean knowing how to create oneself.

pl-l3d14c1-d1e148.summary: Answers that Christ's soul, by wisdom given by grace in the Word to which it is united and which it perfectly understands, knows all that God knows, but cannot do all God can, nor grasp all things as clearly and plainly as God. So it is not equal to its Creator in knowledge, though it knows all he knows, and its wisdom is not equal to God's, which is far worthier and grasps things more perfectly. God thus has greater sufficiency in knowledge than that soul, though it is worthier than every creature.
claims: Christ's soul knows all God knows.
It does not know as clearly as God, so is not equal to him.
Christ's soul cannot do all God can.

pl-l3d14c1-d1e151.summary: Turns the Apostle's text in Lombard's favor: Paul adds 'we have the Spirit of God', showing that through the Spirit he knew God's depths. That soul had the Spirit above all, given without measure (Jn 3:34), so it had the Spirit's gifts without measure, including wisdom. If it knew some things and not others, its knowledge would have a measure; but it has none, so it knows all.
claims: Christ's soul has the Spirit's gifts without measure.
Knowledge without measure is knowledge of all things.

pl-l3d14c1-d1e163.summary: Adds that Fulgentius, in a sermon, says much to assert that that soul has knowledge of all things, using Col 2:3: in him are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.

pl-l3d14c1-d1e170.summary: Gives a rational proof: no one knows anything his soul does not know; Christ, by common agreement, knows all things; so his soul knows all things.
claims: Whatever Christ knows, his soul knows.

pl-l3d14c1-d1e173.summary: Answers the objection that it would know how to create the world or itself: it has knowledge of creating the world but not power, and of creating the soul; it knows how God created it; so it has knowledge of itself as created, not as to be created, since it is not to be created but already created.
claims: Christ's soul knows how to create but lacks the power to create.
Christ's soul knows itself as created.

pl-l3d14c1.summary: Asks whether Christ's soul, wise by gratuitous wisdom, has wisdom equal to God's and knows all that God knows. Some deny it: no creature equals the Creator, otherwise God would not surpass his creature in every good; Ps 138:6 and 1 Cor 2:10 seem to agree, and if it knew all it would know how to create the world and itself. Lombard answers that Christ's soul, by wisdom given by grace in the Word to which it is united, knows all that God knows, but cannot do all that God can and does not grasp things as clearly as God, so it is not equal. Since the Spirit was given to it without measure, it has knowledge without measure and so knows all (Fulgentius, Col 2:3); whatever Christ knows, his soul knows. It knows how to create the world and how it was created, without the power to create.
claims: Christ's soul knows all that God knows, in the Word.
Christ's soul cannot do all that God can.
Christ's soul does not know as clearly as God and so is not equal to him.
Christ's soul has knowledge without measure.
